title: Rabbi Chanilai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Niddah 43b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.43b.13), speaking in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Shimon. In [Yevamot 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.62b.13), Rabbi Tanchum says in the name of Rabbi Chanilai: “Any Jew who has no wife lives without joy, without blessing.”[^1][^2][^4]

notes.text: The William Davidson digital text of Niddah 43b fully writes Rav Chanilai reporting Rabbi Elazar beRabbi Shimon, supporting Elazar for ר״א. Yevamot 62b has Rabbi Chanilai and כל אדם, “any person,” whereas Hyman supplies “any Jew.” The differing full title forms and Hyman’s narrower wording remain explicit.

The checked Niddah 43b fully writes Rav Chanilai reporting Rabbi Elazar beRabbi Shimon; Yevamot 62b fully writes Rabbi Chanilai and says “any person.” Hyman’s “any Jew” and his source-specific abbreviated title are preserved. The two fully written title forms are not automatically harmonized.
At [Yevamot 62b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.62b.13), the consulted text says “any person” and continues “without goodness.” Hyman’s shorter wording is retained.

The linked Niddah passage calls him Rav Chanilai and attributes the teaching to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon. The ruling distinguishes the person who emits semen from someone who touches it. Yevamot uses the title Rabbi for Chanilai.
